monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.body: The monitor turns each frame prepared by the graphics card into millions of pixels on screen.
monitor.fact: 165 Hz means 165 screen refreshes per second. FPS measures frames produced by the GPU; they are separate metrics.

keyboard.title: Keyboard
keyboard.body: When a key is pressed, the keyboard controller sends its code to the computer — a letter, digit or command.
keyboard.fact: A mechanical keyboard has an individual switch under every key.

rgb.label: Lighting
rgb.value: Per-key RGB, can be turned off

mouse.title: Mouse
mouse.body: An optical sensor photographs the desk surface thousands of times per second to calculate movement.
mouse.fact: DPI tells how many pixels the cursor moves when the mouse travels one inch.

pc.title: System unit
pc.body: Inside the case the processor, memory, graphics card, storage and power supply work together.
pc.fact: Cool air enters at the front and hot air leaves at the back and top — a directed airflow.

inside.label: Inside
inside.value: Motherboard, CPU, RAM, GPU, SSD, PSU

inside.title: Inside the case
inside.body: The glass panel is off. Every component plugs into the motherboard and works as one system.
inside.fact: Routing cables behind the motherboard tray improves airflow.

exploded.title: What is a computer made of?
exploded.body: Keep scrolling to look at the components one by one. Click any of them and the camera moves in.

motherboard.name: Motherboard
motherboard.short: The main board that connects every component.
motherboard.body: The processor, memory, graphics card and storage all plug into the motherboard. Data moves between them over the board's buses.

cpu.name: Processor (CPU)
cpu.short: The computer's "brain" — it performs every calculation.
cpu.body: The processor executes program instructions billions of times per second. More cores let it run more tasks at once.

cooler.name: CPU cooler
cooler.short: Removes the processor's heat with a heatsink and fan.
cooler.body: Heat travels through copper heat pipes into aluminium fins, and the fan blows air across them.

ram.name: Memory (RAM)
ram.short: Temporarily holds running programs and their data.
ram.body: RAM is very fast but temporary: everything in it is lost when the computer turns off.

gpu.name: Graphics card (GPU)
gpu.body: A GPU has thousands of small cores, so it computes pixels in parallel. It matters for games, 3D and AI.

ssd.name: NVMe SSD
ssd.short: Fast storage that permanently keeps the OS and files.
ssd.body: An M.2 NVMe SSD stores data in flash memory and talks over PCIe. With no moving parts it is far faster than an HDD.

psu.name: Power supply (PSU)
psu.short: Turns mains power into the voltages components need.
psu.body: The PSU converts alternating current into steady 12 V, 5 V and 3.3 V and delivers it to each part through cables.

fans.name: Case fans
fans.short: Bring cool air into the case and push hot air out.
fans.body: Front fans pull air in and the rear fan exhausts hot air, so components do not overheat.

monitor.name: Monitor
monitor.description: A device that shows the text, pictures and video processed by the computer. The screen is made of millions of tiny dots called pixels.
monitor.purpose: It lets the user see the result of the computer’s work. A monitor is an output device.
monitor.compat: The monitor plugs into a port on the graphics card (or the graphics built into the processor), so both need the same connector, such as HDMI or DisplayPort. The graphics card must also support the monitor’s resolution and refresh rate.

q1.question: What type of device is a monitor?
q1.explain: A monitor sends information from the computer out to the user.

q2.question: What does “1920 × 1080” mean?
q2.c: The number of pixels: width × height
q2.explain: This is the resolution: 1920 pixels across and 1080 pixels down.

q3.question: How many times per second does a 144 Hz monitor refresh the image?
q3.explain: 1 Hz means once per second. A higher rate makes motion look smoother.

keyboard.name: Keyboard
keyboard.description: A device for entering text, numbers and commands. When a key is pressed, the keyboard’s controller sends its code to the computer.
keyboard.purpose: For typing text, writing programs and giving commands with shortcuts (for example, Ctrl + C). A keyboard is an input device.
keyboard.compat: A keyboard connects through a USB port or Bluetooth. To type Kazakh letters (ә, ғ, қ, ң, ө, ұ, ү, һ, і), the Kazakh layout must be added in the operating system.

q1.question: What type of device is a keyboard?
q1.explain: A keyboard puts information into the computer.

q2.question: What does the Ctrl + C shortcut do?
q2.explain: Ctrl + C copies and Ctrl + V pastes.

q3.question: What is under each key of a mechanical keyboard?
q3.explain: Mechanical keyboards have a switch for every key; membrane keyboards use one shared rubber layer.

mouse.name: Mouse
mouse.description: A pointing device that moves the cursor on the screen. Its optical sensor photographs the desk surface thousands of times per second to work out the movement.
mouse.purpose: For selecting objects, clicking buttons, dragging and scrolling pages. A mouse is an input device.

buttons.label: Buttons
buttons.value: Left, right, wheel and extra buttons

mouse.compat: A mouse works with any modern computer through USB or Bluetooth. Setting up extra buttons may require the manufacturer’s software.

q1.question: What does DPI show?
q1.c: How many pixels the cursor moves when the mouse moves 1 inch
q1.explain: DPI stands for dots per inch.

q2.question: Which group of devices does a mouse belong to?
q2.explain: A mouse sends the cursor position and clicks into the computer.

q3.question: How does an optical mouse detect movement?
q3.a: It takes fast pictures of the surface and compares them
q3.explain: Ball mice were used in the past; today a sensor compares pictures of the surface.

headset.name: Headset
headset.description: A device that plays sound only for the user. Headphones with a microphone are called a headset: it is both an output and an input device.
headset.purpose: For music and video, and for talking in online lessons and games, without disturbing people nearby.
headset.compat: Headphones with a 3.5 mm plug go into the audio jack of the sound card or motherboard. Some laptops share one jack for headphones and microphone, which needs a 4-contact (TRRS) plug. USB and Bluetooth headsets do not need an audio jack.

q1.question: What are headphones with a microphone called?
q1.explain: A headset both plays sound and records your voice.

q2.question: Roughly which frequencies can people hear?
q2.explain: That is why headphones are usually designed for this range.

q3.question: How do Bluetooth headphones connect to a computer?

microphone.name: Microphone
microphone.description: A device that turns sound waves into an electrical signal. The computer converts this signal into digital audio.
microphone.purpose: For recording your voice, video calls, online lessons and voice control. A microphone is an input device.

connection.label: Connection
connection.value: USB, 3.5 mm, XLR (through an audio interface)

microphone.compat: A USB microphone plugs straight into the computer. A professional XLR microphone needs an audio interface (an external sound card), and an XLR condenser microphone also needs +48 V phantom power.

q1.question: What type of device is a microphone?
q1.explain: A microphone puts sound into the computer.

q2.question: What does a microphone turn sound into?
q2.explain: A thin diaphragm vibrates with the sound and creates an electrical signal.

q3.question: What do you need to connect an XLR microphone to a computer?
q3.explain: An audio interface amplifies the XLR signal and turns it into digital data.

webcam.name: Webcam
webcam.description: A device that records video and sends it to the computer in real time. The lens focuses light onto a light-sensitive sensor.
webcam.purpose: For video calls, online lessons, streaming and recording video. A webcam is an input device.
webcam.compat: A webcam connects over USB. Many models follow the UVC standard, so they work without an extra driver. Laptops usually have a camera built into the screen frame.

q1.question: What type of device is a webcam?
q1.explain: A webcam puts video into the computer.

q2.question: What resolution is “1080p”?
q2.explain: 1080 is the number of rows of pixels; the width is 1920.

q3.question: How is a webcam usually connected?
q3.explain: SATA is for drives and PCIe x16 is for graphics cards.

speaker.name: Speakers
speaker.description: A device that turns an electrical signal into sound. The speaker cone vibrates and moves the air, which we hear as sound.
speaker.purpose: So several people in a room can hear the sound: music, films, presentations. Speakers are output devices.
speaker.compat: Speakers connect with a 3.5 mm cable to the audio output (the green jack). Active speakers have a built-in amplifier, so they need power from a wall socket or USB.

q1.question: What type of device is a speaker?
q1.explain: Speakers send sound from the computer to the listener.

q2.question: What does “.1” mean in a “2.1” system?
q2.explain: 2 means two main speakers and 1 means a subwoofer for bass.

q3.question: What colour is the usual audio output for speakers?
q3.explain: Green is audio out, pink is the microphone and blue is line in.

printer.name: Printer
printer.description: A device that prints text and pictures on paper. An inkjet printer sprays tiny drops of ink, while a laser printer fuses toner powder onto the paper with heat.
printer.purpose: For printing documents, reports, photos and tickets. A printer is an output device.

speed.label: Speed
speed.value: Usually 10–30 pages per minute for home printers

printer.compat: A printer connects over USB or a network (Wi-Fi, Ethernet), and its driver must be installed in the operating system. Each model only takes its own cartridges or toner.

q1.question: What type of device is a printer?
q1.explain: A printer outputs information on paper. A scanner, by contrast, is an input device.

q2.question: What does a laser printer use to put the image on paper?
q2.explain: The toner sticks to the paper and is fixed by heated rollers.

q3.question: What must be installed on the computer for a printer to work?
q3.explain: A driver is a program that tells the operating system how to work with a device.

motherboard.name: Motherboard
motherboard.description: The main circuit board that connects every part of the computer. It holds the processor socket, memory slots, expansion slots, ports and the chipset.
motherboard.purpose: It links the parts together, carrying data between them and sharing out power from the power supply.

socket.label: CPU socket
socket.value: For example AMD AM4, AM5, Intel LGA1700

expansion.label: Expansion
expansion.value: PCIe x16, PCIe x1, M.2, SATA

motherboard.compat: The motherboard socket must match the processor and its memory slots must match the RAM type (DDR4 or DDR5). The board’s form factor must fit the case: an ATX board will not fit in a Mini-ITX case.

q1.question: Where on the motherboard is the processor installed?
q1.explain: The socket is a special seat made for the processor.

q2.question: Can DDR5 memory go into a board that only has DDR4 slots?
q2.a: Yes, if the board is new
q2.b: No, the key notch and standard are different
q2.explain: The notch on the module stops the wrong memory type from being inserted.

q3.question: What size is a standard ATX motherboard?

cpu.name: Processor (CPU)
cpu.description: The central processing unit that carries out program instructions. Inside are the arithmetic logic unit, the control unit and fast cache memory.
cpu.purpose: It does all the calculations and logic operations and directs the other parts of the computer. It is often called the computer’s “brain”.

cache.label: Cache
cache.value: L1, L2, L3 — from a few to tens of MB

cpu.compat: A processor only fits a motherboard with the matching socket: an AM5 processor needs an AM5 board. The board’s chipset and BIOS version must support the processor, and the cooler must handle its heat (TDP).

q1.question: What does CPU stand for?
q1.explain: It is the central unit that processes data.

q2.question: What unit is processor clock speed measured in?
q2.explain: 1 GHz is one billion clock cycles per second.

q3.question: What should you check first when choosing a motherboard for a processor?
q3.explain: If the socket does not match, the processor physically will not fit.

ram.name: Memory (RAM)
ram.description: Fast memory that temporarily holds the programs and data the processor is using right now. Its contents are lost when the computer is switched off.
ram.purpose: It feeds data to the processor much faster than a drive can. More memory lets you keep more programs and browser tabs open at once.

capacity.label: Capacity
capacity.value: Usually 8–32 GB; one module is 8, 16 or 32 GB

ram.compat: The memory type must match the motherboard: DDR4 and DDR5 modules have the notch in different places, so they do not fit each other’s slots. For dual channel, install two identical modules in the slots named in the board’s manual.

q1.question: What happens to the data in RAM when the computer is switched off?
q1.a: It is sent to the printer
q1.explain: RAM is volatile memory. Files are kept on an SSD or HDD.

q2.question: What is RAM for?
q2.a: To hold the data the processor is working on for a short time
q2.b: To keep files for a long time
q2.c: To show the picture on screen
q2.explain: Long-term storage is the drive’s job, and showing pictures is the graphics card’s job.

q3.question: Can a DDR4 module go into a DDR5 slot?
q3.explain: The notch is in a different place, so the module will not go in.

gpu.name: Graphics card (GPU)
gpu.description: A device that processes images, 3D graphics and video and sends them to the monitor. Its graphics processor has thousands of small cores working in parallel.
gpu.purpose: For games, 3D modelling, video editing and artificial intelligence calculations. Monitors plug into its ports.
gpu.compat: A graphics card goes into the PCIe x16 slot on the motherboard. It must be short enough for the case, and the power supply needs enough wattage and the right extra power cables (8 or 16 pins).

q1.question: Which motherboard slot does a graphics card go into?
q1.explain: DIMM slots are for memory and SATA is for drives.

q2.question: What is a graphics card’s own memory called?
q2.explain: VRAM stores textures and the frames shown on screen.

q3.question: What else should you check when installing a powerful graphics card?
q3.a: The power supply wattage and the case length
q3.explain: Without enough power, the computer can shut down under load.

ssd.name: Solid-state drive (SSD)
ssd.description: A drive that stores data on flash memory chips. It has no moving parts, so it is fast, silent and resistant to knocks.
ssd.purpose: For long-term storage of the operating system, programs and files. Data stays saved after the computer is switched off.

speed.label: Read speed
speed.value: SATA — up to 550 MB/s; NVMe — 3500–7000 MB/s

ssd.compat: An M.2 SSD needs an M.2 slot on the motherboard that supports its type (NVMe or SATA). A 2.5-inch SATA SSD connects to the board with a SATA cable and to the power supply with a SATA power cable.

q1.question: Where does an SSD store data?
q1.explain: A spinning magnetic disk is how an HDD works.

q2.question: Why is an SSD faster than an HDD?
q2.c: It has no moving mechanical parts
q2.explain: An HDD must wait for its head to reach the right spot; an SSD has no such wait.

q3.question: What does “2280” mean in “M.2 2280”?
q3.explain: The first two digits are the width and the rest is the length, in millimetres.

hdd.name: Hard disk drive (HDD)
hdd.description: A drive that stores data on spinning magnetic platters. A read/write head moves just above the surface of the disk.
hdd.purpose: For storing large amounts of data, such as photos, videos and archives, at a low price.
hdd.compat: An HDD connects to a SATA port on the motherboard with a data cable and to the power supply with a SATA power cable. A 3.5-inch drive needs a matching bay in the case.

q1.question: Where does an HDD store data?
q1.explain: The direction of magnetisation stores the 0s and 1s.

q2.question: What is the main advantage of an HDD over an SSD?
q2.explain: An SSD wins on speed and shock resistance.

q3.question: Why should you not shake a running HDD?
q3.c: The head could scratch the platter and damage data
q3.explain: The gap between the head and the platter is thinner than a human hair.

psu.name: Power supply unit (PSU)
psu.description: A device that turns 220–230 V alternating current from the wall socket into the steady DC voltages computer parts need (+12 V, +5 V, +3.3 V).
psu.purpose: It gives every part a steady and safe supply of power.

efficiency.label: Efficiency
efficiency.value: 80 PLUS rating: White, Bronze, Gold, Platinum

psu.compat: The power supply should have about 20–30 % more wattage than all the parts use together. It needs the right connectors for the graphics card and processor, and its form factor (ATX or SFX) must fit the case.

q1.question: What does a power supply do?
q1.c: Turns AC from the wall into steady DC voltages
q1.explain: Computer parts run only on DC voltage.

q2.question: How many pins does the main motherboard power connector have?
q2.explain: That is why it is called the “24-pin ATX” connector.

q3.question: What does an “80 PLUS Gold” label show?
q3.explain: Higher efficiency means less electricity is wasted as heat.

cooler.name: CPU cooler
cooler.description: A cooling system that carries heat away from the processor. Heat travels through copper heat pipes into aluminium fins, and a fan blows air across them.
cooler.purpose: It stops the processor from overheating. When too hot, the processor slows itself down or the computer shuts off to protect itself.

paste.label: Thermal paste
paste.value: Goes between the processor and the cooler base

cooler.compat: The cooler’s mounting must fit the processor socket (for example AM5 or LGA1700) and it must be short enough for the case. It must be able to remove at least as much heat as the processor’s TDP.

q1.question: What goes between the processor and the cooler base?
q1.explain: Thermal paste fills tiny gaps and conducts heat well.

q2.question: What metal are heat pipes usually made of?
q2.explain: Copper conducts heat very well and is far cheaper than gold.

q3.question: What happens if the processor overheats?
q3.b: It slows down or the computer shuts off
q3.explain: This is a safety feature that protects the processor from damage.

fans.name: Case fans
fans.description: Fans that refresh the air inside the case. Front fans pull cool air in, while rear and top fans push hot air out.
fans.purpose: They lower the temperature of every part, helping them run reliably and last longer.
fans.compat: The fan size must match the mounting spot in the case (120 or 140 mm). With a 4-pin (PWM) fan, the motherboard sets the speed automatically based on temperature.

q1.question: What do the front case fans usually do?
q1.explain: Hot air rises, so the rear and top fans push it out.

q2.question: What is the advantage of a 4-pin (PWM) fan?
q2.a: The motherboard can control its speed
q2.explain: Under light load the fan spins slowly and quietly.

q3.question: What size are case fans most often?
q3.explain: The size is the width of the fan frame in millimetres.

nic.name: Network card (NIC)
nic.description: A device that connects the computer to a local network and the internet. Every network adapter has a unique physical address called a MAC address.
nic.purpose: For sending and receiving data over a network: the internet, file sharing, online games.

interface.label: Installation
interface.value: Built into the board or a separate PCIe card

nic.compat: Many motherboards already have a network adapter built in. A separate card goes into a free PCIe slot. The real speed also depends on the cable (for example Cat5e, Cat6) and the router.

q1.question: What is the unique physical address of a network adapter called?
q1.explain: The MAC address is set at the factory; an IP address is assigned by the network.

q2.question: Which port does an Ethernet cable plug into?

q3.question: Where does a separate network card go on the motherboard?
q3.explain: Network, sound and graphics cards are all PCIe expansion cards.

assistant.title: AI assistant
assistant.welcome: Tell me your budget, purpose and the devices you want. I build a compatible setup from catalog products only, explain each choice and load it into Setup Studio.
assistant.exampleDevices: ASUS 300 Hz monitor and Logitech mouse
assistant.placeholder: For example: 800k for gaming and study…
assistant.overBudget: These requirements exceed your budget by {amount}. Increase the budget or relax the device requirements.
assistant.unavailable: Not in the catalog: {items}. This requirement was not met.
assistant.invalid: A complete compatible build was not found. Change the budget or requirements.
assistant.privacy: If the AI server is connected, the request goes only to it (no API key in the browser); otherwise it is handled on this device. Prices are demo values.

reasons.gaming: Most of the budget goes to the GPU, balanced with the CPU, power supply and monitor.
reasons.study: An economical system with enough memory and SSD space. A separate GPU is omitted when integrated graphics suffice.
reasons.programming: The CPU, memory and SSD take priority for coding and multitasking.
reasons.design3d: The CPU, GPU and memory take priority for rendering and 3D work.
reasons.streaming: The GPU and CPU cover gaming and encoding, with a headset for audio.
reasons.universal: A balanced budget allocation across the CPU, graphics, memory and monitor.

fallback.unavailable: AI server unavailable — the local engine answered.
fallback.invalid: The AI answer failed validation — the local engine answered.

assistant.loaded: Loaded into Setup Studio — shown in 3D

improve.prompt: Improve this setup for my budget and purpose

cpu.study: CPU — {model} ({cores}): fast and efficient for study, {share}% of the budget.
cpu.programming: CPU — {model} ({cores}): compiling and multitasking scale with cores, so it comes first.
cpu.design3d: CPU — {model} ({cores}): rendering and 3D work use every core.
cpu.streaming: CPU — {model} ({cores}): handles the game and the stream at once.
cpu.universal: CPU — {model} ({cores}): a balanced choice for study, code and games.

gpu.study: Graphics card — {model} ({vram}): the budget allowed it, useful for video and 3D lessons.
gpu.programming: Graphics card — {model} ({vram}): after CPU and memory; helps with ML and graphics.
gpu.design3d: Graphics card — {model} ({vram}): speeds up the viewport and GPU rendering, {share}% of the budget.
gpu.streaming: Graphics card — {model} ({vram}): runs the game and encodes the stream.
gpu.universal: Graphics card — {model} ({vram}): a solid middle ground for games and graphics.
